learning_objectives: Identify the stem of a regular -are verb by removing -are.
Produce all six affirmative present indicative forms with the endings -o, -i, -a, -iamo, -ate and -ano.
Use regular -are present forms in short statements about current activities and routines.

skills.description_en: Identify the stem of a regular -are infinitive by removing -are.
Recall the six present indicative endings for regular -are verbs.
Choose the present form that agrees with the subject in person and number.
Use regular -are present forms for simple current activities and routines.
Produce short affirmative A1 sentences with regular -are verbs in the present indicative.

lesson.short_explanation_en: Regular Italian verbs ending in -are belong to the first conjugation. To build the present indicative, remove -are to find the stem, then add the ending for the subject: -o, -i, -a, -iamo, -ate, -ano. For example, parlare → parl- → parlo, parli, parla, parliamo, parlate, parlano. Italian often omits the subject pronoun because the verb ending already shows the person. This lesson uses the present for simple current activities and routines only.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: For a straightforward regular -are verb, remove the infinitive ending -are. The part that remains is the stem used in this lesson.
usage_notes_en: Use simple regular examples here so spelling-change rules do not distract from the core pattern.
common_errors_en: Do not keep -are before adding the present ending: *parlareo is not a form.
Do not treat irregular verbs such as fare or andare as if they followed this pattern.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: Add -o, -i, -a, -iamo, -ate or -ano according to person and number.
rule_blocks.pattern: io -o | tu -i | lui/lei -a | noi -iamo | voi -ate | loro -ano
usage_notes_en: Subject pronouns are often omitted when the verb ending makes the subject clear.
common_errors_en: Do not use -ate for noi; noi takes -iamo.
Do not use -a for a plural subject; loro takes -ano.

rule_blocks.heading_en: Use the present for simple current activities and routines
rule_blocks.explanation_en: At this stage, use these forms for actions or situations that are current, regular or habitual.
rule_blocks.pattern: Lavoro in ufficio. / La sera ascoltano la radio.
usage_notes_en: Time expressions such as ogni giorno, la mattina and la sera can make a routine clear.
common_errors_en: Do not introduce past or future meanings in this lesson.

contexts.setting_en: Anna and Marco talk about their everyday work and language habits.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.target: Lavoro in ufficio e abito in città.
lines.translation_en: I work in an office and live in the city.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Io lavoro a casa e parlo italiano ogni giorno.
lines.translation_en: I work at home and speak Italian every day.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.translation_en: I speak Italian with a friend.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.translation_en: I listen to the radio in the morning.

focus_items.explanation_en: Lavoro has the regular first-person singular ending -o.
Abito has the regular first-person singular ending -o.
Parlo is formed from parl- plus -o.
Ascolto is formed from ascolt- plus -o.

contexts.setting_en: A short description of two people during a normal day.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.translation_en: In the evening they listen to the radio.

focus_items.explanation_en: Lavora uses the third-person singular ending -a.
Abitano uses the third-person plural ending -ano.
Parlano uses the third-person plural ending -ano.
Ascoltano uses the third-person plural ending -ano.

examples.note_en: The regular present can describe a current routine or normal activity.
abit- takes the first-person plural ending -iamo.

examples.translation_en: You all listen to the radio.
examples.note_en: ascolt- takes the second-person plural ending -ate.
ascolt- takes the third-person singular ending -a.
